codeReview.summary: The memory consolidation feature is correctly implemented in commit 8b3214c (NOT the handoff-referenced c62347d which contains self_improve code). The implementation creates core/memory/consolidation.py with MemoryConsolidator class implementing all three required operations: merge (>0.9 cosine similarity), confidence decay (×0.95 for 30+ days unaccessed), and prune (confidence <0.1 and age >90 days). Deduplication before store (>0.95 similarity) is implemented via check_duplicate_before_store() and integrated into MemoryManager.store(). Celery Beat task registered at 3:00 AM EAT. All 18 tests pass against real PostgreSQL with pgvector. The intelligence-scan was sensibly moved from 3:00 AM to 3:15 AM to avoid overlap. Verified memories are protected from decay, pruning, and being merged away. IMPORTANT: The handoff file references the wrong commit (c62347d is self_improve, not consolidation). The actual consolidation commit is 8b3214c.

issues.description: _get_session() creates a new async engine on every call. The consolidation pipeline calls merge, decay, and prune sequentially — each creates its own engine+session. The rest of the codebase uses AsyncSessionLocal (a shared session factory). Creating 3 engines per consolidation run is wasteful and could leak connections if errors occur between engine creation and the finally block. Should use AsyncSessionLocal for consistency.

merge_similar_memories() fetches ALL memories with embeddings into memory at once (line 126-131), then runs a separate pgvector similarity query per memory (O(N²) database round-trips). The batch_size parameter is accepted but never actually used for pagination. For tables with thousands of memories, this will be slow and memory-intensive. Consider processing in batches or using a self-join approach.

Combined confidence formula: survivor + sum(deleted.confidence * 0.5). The 0.5 multiplier is undocumented and not specified in the feature requirements. The spec says 'combined confidence' which could mean a straight sum (capped at 1.0). The current formula discounts merged memories' contributions by 50%, which is a reasonable design choice but should be documented.

The memory-prune task (2 AM) in MemoryManager.prune() already performs confidence decay (×0.95 for 30+ days) and deletion of low-confidence old memories — identical logic to what MemoryConsolidator.apply_confidence_decay() and prune_old_memories() do at 3 AM. This means stale memories get decayed TWICE daily (effective decay = 0.95² ≈ 0.9025 per day instead of 0.95). The prune task should either be updated to skip decay/delete (deferring to consolidation) or the consolidation should skip those steps.
